cards.headline: From deciding to owning.
cards.body: You've built the judgment. A trade is just the mechanical step that turns a decision into ownership — it runs through a {{term:broker|broker}} in a handful of taps.

art.alt: A broker passing a customer's buy order along to the market on their behalf.

cards.headline: First, an account to trade from.
cards.body: A {{term:brokerage-account|brokerage account}} is where you hold and trade investments. Opening one resembles opening a bank account: a little ID, a few minutes, and a transfer to fund it.

cards.headline: Find the company's ticker.
cards.body: Every listed stock has a {{term:ticker-symbol|ticker symbol}} — a short code like AAPL or KO. You type that ticker to pull up its order ticket.

cards.headline: The real choice: how to price it.
cards.body: The order ticket's key question is how you want to buy. The first two you'll meet — a **market order** and a **limit order** — trade certainty of price against certainty of getting filled.

art.alt: A balance weighing certainty of getting filled against certainty of the exact price paid.

cards.headline: Market order: fill it now.
cards.body: A {{term:market-order|market order}} buys straight away at the best price available. You're almost sure to get the shares, but in fast markets the exact price can shift as it fills.

cards.headline: Limit order: name your price.
cards.body: A {{term:limit-order|limit order}} sets the most you'll pay. It fills only at your price or better — shielding you from surprises, but it may not fill at all if the price runs away.

cards.prompt: You want to own a stock today and don't mind a few cents of drift in the price. Which order fits best?

options.label: Limit order — prioritize an exact price

cards.explanation: A **market order** trades a little price precision for near-certain execution — right when simply owning it matters more than the last few cents. Reach for a **limit order** when the price you pay is the priority.

cards.headline: Read the ticket before you tap buy.
cards.body: Before you submit, the ticket shows a summary: ticker, number of shares, order type, and estimated cost. Read it once — most first-trade mistakes are a wrong number here, not a wrong idea.
If it matters that you never pay more than a set price, you'd place a [[1]] order.
cards.explanation: A **limit order** caps your price — it fills only at your number or better. A market order takes the going price; a stop order is a trigger to trade later.

cards.summary: A first trade is a short, calm checklist — not a leap. Fund an account, find the ticker, pick your order type, review, submit.
bullets: Open and fund a brokerage account.
Look up the ticker to open the order ticket.
Choose market or limit, review the summary, then submit.

art.alt: An order travelling from a phone through the broker to the exchange, where it is matched.

cards.insight: The hard part of investing is the thinking. The trade itself is a few taps and one careful second look.
